name: Max to the Right of Min
description: You are given a permutation $$$p$$$ of length $$$n$$$ — an array, consisting of integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, all distinct. Let $$$p_{l,r}$$$ denote a subarray — an array formed by writing down elements from index $$$l$$$ to index $$$r$$$, inclusive. Let $$$\mathit{maxpos}_{l,r}$$$ denote the index of the maximum element on $$$p_{l,r}$$$. Similarly, let $$$\mathit{minpos}_{l,r}$$$ denote the index of the minimum element on it. Calculate the number of subarrays $$$p_{l,r}$$$ such that $$$\mathit{maxpos}_{l,r} \gt \mathit{minpos}_{l,r}$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the number of elements in the permutation. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$). All $$$p_i$$$ are distinct.
output_specification: Print a single integer — the number of subarrays $$$p_{l,r}$$$ such that $$$\mathit{maxpos}_{l,r} \gt \mathit{minpos}_{l,r}$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.
